prose_updates.related_work: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) supply the fixed-grid latent-factor survival panel, unit and time spans, PCR transport, and the 925-patient, 10-country TCL application. They already assume event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates; the present advance is therefore not a weaker censoring premise, but replacement of marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier inputs by covariate-adjusted AIPCW inputs when within-cell covariate heterogeneity creates marginal dependent censoring, together with full transported inference. Proposition~\ref{prop:han-shah-fixed-grid-embedding} gives the exact matrix bridge from their spans to \(y\in\operatorname{row}(M)\) and \(yM_r^+B\), while Proposition~\ref{prop:km-pcr-cancellation} certifies an open class of fixed Kaplan--Meier/PCR bias. Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024, published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4) and Sections 5.2--5.3) supply the cross-fitted augmented survival-score architecture and direct-curve asymptotic linearity, but not a data-dependent spectral transport. The relative-survival variation restriction imposed here is an additional primitive sufficient condition not imposed by Westling et al.; they instead assume the exact Stieltjes-remainder rate. Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025, Theorem 2 and Corollary 2) clarify minimum-norm PCR and row-space prediction without censoring-aware asymptotics. Golub and Pereyra (1973, equation (4.12)) are the matrix-calculus ancestor for the constant-rank pseudoinverse derivative. Curth, Poon, Nori, and Gonz\'alez (2024, Sections 3--4) analyze survival synthetic-control bias but do not derive this three-block PCR pseudo-limit or its relatively open nonzero-bias region. Fan and Liao (2022) study growing-panel factor models, while Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2026) study robustness to rank misspecification. These are neighboring problems: this note leaves weak-gap and selected-rank inference for the unregularized fixed-donor pseudoinverse target as an acknowledged open frontier.

statement_notes.gap: Fan and Liao (2022, Theorem 2.1 and Theorem 3.2 with Corollary 3.1; arXiv v3, pp. 10--11 and 20--21) study growing-panel factor models, including factor-space recovery with bounded over-estimated rank as the cross-sectional dimension grows. Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2026) study robustness to rank misspecification for high-dimensional linear functionals. These are neighboring problems, but neither covers a fixed donor panel, an unregularized nonlinear pseudoinverse target, or a local singular collision under orthogonal survival-score noise. Weak-gap and selected-rank inference therefore remains an acknowledged open frontier of this note.
